_about.what: Structure parts (labels, frames, port frames, glass, windows, decoupler) for the blueprint generator. Built by build_structure.py from prefab_dump.json + the 301-blueprint corpus; prose rules come from structure_rules.json. Method and evidence: structure.md.
_about.coordinates: Canonical frame = orientation 16; footprint [0,w)x[0,h)x[0,d); origin = min corner of the rotated footprint (model.py convention, re-verified for frames: all 9,630 frame-quarter-type instances share one 4-grid residue per blueprint across up to 24 orientations). A port is the cell just outside the part ('cell') plus the part cell it touches ('face').
_about.mirrored_twins: '<prefab> M' twins: same orientation codes, everything reflected along local x (x -> w-1-x; continuous coordinates x -> w-x). Verified on the port frames (99 + 70 twin instances, every cable on the reflected port cell) and the decoupler (221 twins).
_about.sizes: Footprint = root EPC_SC* component floats at bytes 12..23 (metres) / 0.125; the float at 24 is the mass in kg. This source reproduces all 43 partdb.json sizes exactly.
_about.solid_cells: Box parts fill their footprint. Curved/partial parts (curved frames, curved glass, curved windows) fill only the cells listed in 'solid_cells' (centre inside or on the hull of the part's face polygons); the rest of the bounding box is free and other parts use it (corpus: every such overlap is >= 0.5 cell outside the hull, except one ducted-fan design).
_about.settings_offsets: Field offsets are those of the current schema (schemas.json). Older saves use shorter records (labels without _labelRotated, frames with a single _col); write the current layout.
_about.status: Priority-1 parts (labels, frame quarter, port frames, glass/frame half) and the frame support rule are done and validated; priority-2 parts have size, canonical orientation, faces/solid cells, twins and corpus counts.

label_rules.footprint: SC_LabelSmall (Label) 2x1x1, SC_LabelMedium (Large Label) 4x1x1 cells: x = text direction, y = text height, z = depth. The visible part is a 0.02 m plate lying flush against the back face (collider centre z = -0.0525 m in a cell spanning -0.0625..0.0625 m).
label_rules.attachment: Only the back face (local -z) has a JointsArea, so a label is held by whatever occupies the cells (x, 0, -1), x = 0..w-1. Corpus: 1,059 of 1,063 Labels have those cells occupied (1,045 fully); the front (+z) is free in 1,046. Typical supports: a frame face (FrameQuarterPorts 799 cells, FrameA 430, FrameQuarterA 20 ...) or the top of a 1-cell logic block (Remapper 284, Constant 189, Fader 104, ...). The 46 Large Labels with nothing behind them are in the pasted modules ('Better Than PID', 'Universal flight computer' + autosaves), whose bottom layer rests on whatever floor the module is pasted onto.
label_rules.text_orientation: Text faces local +z. Its top is local +y when _labelRotated = 0 and local -y when 1. Corpus: vertical labels with _labelRotated = 0 have local +y = world up in 743 of 795 cases (1 upside down); all 13 with _labelRotated = 1 have local +y = world down, i.e. the flag is used to turn upside-down placements upright. Reading direction (from the text renderer transform, euler 270/180/0 applied to the game's +y-facing text mesh, the same mesh as the logic-block captions): along local -x when _labelRotated = 0, so the first character sits at the high-x end; along +x when 1. Corpus support for -x: in 'Universal flight computer' two-label names on one line read naturally only from high x to low x ('AUTO LEVEL' + 'SENSITIVITY', 'ON/OFF AUTO' + 'PLANET TRAVEL'), and in 'Multiplexer' the labels '2    1' (low x) and '4    3' (high x) put the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 in increasing x only if the text runs along -x. Not yet seen in game: medium-high confidence.
label_rules.orientation_choice: World text normal = R_k*(0,0,1); text up = R_k*(0,1,0) and reading direction = R_k*(-1,0,0), both negated when _labelRotated = 1 (R_k from orientations.json). Upright label on a vertical wall facing world n: 16 (n = +z), 21 (-z), 3 (+x), 6 (-x); all have R_k*(0,1,0) = (0,1,0). Label lying on a floor facing up: 8, 9, 10 or 11 (R_k*(0,0,1) = (0,1,0)); text top = R_k*(0,1,0): 8 -> -z, 9 -> +z, 10 -> +x, 11 -> -x. 'orientation_table' lists front/up/reading direction for all 24 codes. A label in an upside-down orientation can be made upright with _labelRotated = 1 instead of re-orienting.
label_rules.text_limits: Label: 14 characters (_maxLength = 14), Large Label: 16 (_maxLength = 16). The blueprint field is 32 bytes UTF-16LE (16 code units) zero-padded; never exceed the per-label limit. All 7,962 corpus text fields (labels and every other part title) are upper case (A-Z, 0-9, space and % + , - . / :), so upper-case the text.
label_rules.placement_at_cable_ends: Both glass-encased examples put one Large Label per I/O cable end: the label lies on the cable's axis immediately beyond the end cell (the last, straight cable cell, which sits one cell outside the glass), long axis along the cable, in the same layer. 'Better Than PID': cable ends (196..198, 20, 203), labels at z = 199..202 (orientation 10, flat, text facing world +y). 'Universal flight computer': ends at z = 175 and z = 184, labels at z = 171..174 and 185..188 (orientation 10 flat, or 6 standing and facing world -x). All 16 labelled cable ends follow this; the label's x end touches the cable cell (cable at label-local (4,0,0) or (-1,0,0)). Neighbouring cable ends get neighbouring labels (one row per cable), and a longer name continues with a second label further along the same line ('ON/OFF AUTO' then 'PLANET TRAVEL'). The label covers the cell where the cable would continue, so the user removes it or connects past it; for the generator a label beside the end cell (not on its axis) works just as well as long as its back face is supported.
label_rules.placement_on_port_frames: Most common labelling of a Frame Quarter With Ports (372 corpus labels): four 2-cell Labels on the port face, backs against the frame, in the outer ring of the 4x4 face next to the 2x2 port block, one per port: frame-local cells (0..1, 0) under port A, (2..3, 0) under B, (2..3, 3) over C, (0..1, 3) over D, at z = -1 for the side-0 face (z = 4 for side 1). They do not cover port cells. Counts: (2..3,3) 118, (0..1,0) 105, (2..3,0) 75, (0..1,3) 74. Text upright in world terms (choose k / _labelRotated so the text top is world up).
label_rules.struct: EPC_SCLabel+Blueprint+BlueprintData (90ef24df4ed7024b), 58 bytes: _guid 0 (16), _actionableLabel 16 (32), _gt 48 (4), _col 52 (1), _labelRotated 53 (write 1 byte, zeros after). _col: 0 unpainted/default (795 of 1,063), 2 the next most common.

frame_ports_rules.ports: Frame Quarter With Ports: 8 ports in the centre 2x2 of two opposite faces. Side 0 on -z: port cells (1,1,-1) A, (2,1,-1) B, (2,2,-1) C, (1,2,-1) D; side 1 on +z: the same x,y at z = 4. Corner variant: side 0 on +x: (4,1,1) A, (4,1,2) B, (4,2,2) C, (4,2,1) D; side 1 on +z: (1,1,4) A, (2,1,4) B, (2,2,4) C, (1,2,4) D. Mirrored twins reflect x: the straight twin keeps the same cells with A<->B and C<->D swapped; the corner twin's side 0 moves to the -x face (cells (-1,y,z)).
frame_ports_rules.pairing: Port i is linked to port i+4 through the wall: A0-A1, B0-B1, C0-C1, D0-D1. Source: SCTick_FrameWithPorts+SharePortsValuesJob.Execute loops i = 0..3 over ownPorts[i] and ownPorts[i+4] (burst.asm line 730713 ff., loads at [buf+i*8] and [buf+i*8+0x20]); the prefab port list is A0 B0 C0 D0 A1 B1 C1 D1. Straight frame: each pair goes straight through along z at the same (x,y). Corner frame: the +x-face port at (y, z) pairs with the +z-face port at (x = z, y), a 90-degree turn about y. Corpus: whenever both ends of a pair carry a cable they are the same kind (data/data or power/power) in 1,152 of 1,152 cases; every other pairing of the 8 ports mixes kinds 26-54% of the time.
frame_ports_rules.kinds: All 8 ports are type 5 = universal/unset in the prefab port list (logic inputs are type 0, outputs 1, power 2, wireless 3, plasma 4). The game sets each port's runtime type from what is plugged in and has port meshes for data (InOut), power, plasma and unset. Corpus: data and power cables both land on all 8 positions of both variants (the prefab child names such as 'Port D Power1' are leftovers: D takes data 87 times). Plasma: no corpus case (only 83 plasma cable cells exist); supported per the plasma port mesh.
frame_ports_rules.direction: No fixed direction ('both'). A pair passes a data value from the driven side to the other, and is only active when both ports of the pair are connected (the job skips a pair if either port's _persistentConnectedCCOrPort is null). Power through a pair behaves as a 4-cell cable ('Each connected port pair also consumes 4 cables').
frame_ports_rules.chains: If a frame port touches another frame-with-ports port directly (port cell of one = face cell of the other), SharePortsValuesJob follows the chain: it finds the touching port in the next frame's port buffer, jumps to its partner (index +-4) and copies the value on, frame after frame, while the next connection is again a frame port of the same ship (same Parent). So a row of Frame Quarter With Ports carries cables through a thick wall ('place multiple frames next to each other to route cables through a larger structure', in-game manual). Two straight port frames stacked along their z axis line up A-A, B-B, C-C, D-D automatically. Corpus: 13,760 direct frame-port-to-frame-port contacts (mostly A1-A0, B1-B0, C1-C0, D1-D0 of stacked frames; frames facing each other side 0 to side 0 pair A-A, C-C and B-D).
frame_ports_rules.direct_part_contact: A part's port can also plug straight into a frame port with no cable (the part sits flush against the port face, its port cell = the frame's face cell and vice versa). Corpus: 178 such contacts, e.g. 112 Power Router power ports, 40 Multiplier inputs, 11 Sign Splitter inputs, 4 Data Router 2 outputs. The frame port takes the part port's kind.
frame_ports_rules.cable_rule: A cable joins a frame port like any port: the cable cell in the port cell must open toward the frame (a straight cell along the port axis, or a corner cell with an open face toward the frame). Corpus: 6,825 cable cells open toward the 5,169 port-frame instances (2,829 straight, 3,996 corner) and every one is on a predicted port cell (0 misses).
frame_ports_rules.support: A frame with ports is a full frame: parts attach to all 6 faces and straight cables are anchored along its faces like any frame (frame_support_rules); a welded face does not anchor a cable at a port position (the code re-queries for the port collider there).

frame_support_rules.parts: Parts join each other through touching JointsArea polygons (SpaceshipComponentAreaPoly children). Box frames have a full JointsArea on all 6 faces; curved frames only on their flat faces (none on the slope); a label only on its back; logic blocks on all 6. Welding does not matter for holding parts: a bare frame holds parts on every flat face. JointsArea headers give joint type and material: (0,0) normal, (0,5) glass and windows, (0,4) thrusters/lights/decoupler, (1,0) pipe connections (fuel), (3,4) the decoupler's suction face. In-game manual: 'Always place components on a frame. Cables do not count as support'.
frame_support_rules.welding: The Welder mounts/dismounts a plate on one face of a frame. A blueprint stores this per face in _solidFaces: bit i = face i of the prefab's face list ('faces' in each frame entry; FaceSetupData order, which is the FramePrefabFacesData order the game reads; up to 8 faces, the split triangles of the 8x8 faces count separately). _col0.._col7 colour the same faces (200 = unpainted; slots past the face count stay 200). A fully welded frame weighs twice as much (_fullSolidMass) and is sealed against vacuum and thruster noise. Corpus: no _solidFaces value ever sets a bit at or past the face count (26 frame types, 53,555 records).
frame_support_rules.cable_anchoring_rule: From Burst GarageUpdateCables.UpdateCellsAndPortsJob (read by the power study, power.md Q4, and re-read here at burst.asm 0x180490C20-0x1804913D3): (1) a cable cell joined to a compatible port is anchored. (2) A STRAIGHT cable cell (shape 0; corner cells never) probes the 4 directions perpendicular to its axis, 0.0725 m from its centre. If the probe point is inside a frame collider, the line through the cell centre along the probe is tested against the frame's face polygons in index order (Moller-Trumbore on (v0,v1,v2) and, for quads, (v0,v2,v3); back faces culled, so the face whose outward normal points at the cable, i.e. the near face). The first face hit decides: the cell is anchored if that face's _solidFaces bit is set (on a frame with ports: unless the probe is at a port) or if the hit point is closer than 0.08 m to the line through any edge of that polygon. (3) UpdateAnchoringJob: every cell must be within 10 steps (MAX_UNANCHORED_CELLS = 10) of an anchored cell along its own cable chain, else 'Cannot enter Fly Mode because some cable cells are not anchored'.
frame_support_rules.which_cells_anchor: Cable cells lie one cell outside the face, so the hit point is the projection of the cell centre onto the face: 0.0625 m from the face edge for the outer ring of cells, >= 0.1875 m for every inner cell. Bare (unwelded) face: only the outer ring of cells anchors (12 of the 16 positions of a 4x4 frame-quarter face, 20 of 32 on a 4x8 face, 28 of 64 on an 8x8 face); welded face: every position (except port positions on a port frame's welded port face). Special case, SC_FrameA (8x8x4): each 8x8 face is two triangles, and the diagonal is a polygon edge, so on a bare face the 8 cells on the diagonal also anchor: Z+ face cells with x == y, Z- face cells with x + y == 7 (canonical x,y). The same holds for any face stored as triangles (see 'faces').
frame_support_rules.corpus_evidence: Network test (structure_anchor.py, all 301 blueprints, 219k data/power/plasma cable cells): cable networks with a cell more than 10 steps from every anchor: ports only 1,691; + bare-frame edge rule 44; + welded faces with the FaceSetupData bit order (exact rule) 39; welded faces with the earlier JointsArea-order guess 42; exact rule without the triangle diagonals 41; upper bound (any straight cell whose side touches a frame) 38. The exact rule matches the upper bound except for one network in one autosave. Bit order: among all 720 orderings of the 6 faces of FrameQuarterA/FrameHalfA/FrameQuarterPorts/PortsCorner/Pipe, the FaceSetupData order puts cable contacts on welded faces more often than 95.6-99.9% of orderings. Contacts (straight cell side against a frame face): edge/bare 50,481, edge/welded 19,339, inner/welded 10,359, inner/bare 20,414 (the last are anchored elsewhere within 10 steps).
frame_support_rules.generator: To support cables with a bare frame: run straight cable cells flat along a frame face on its outer ring (the cells one layer outside the face whose projection falls in the face's outer ring) and keep every cell within 10 steps of such a cell or of a port; corners never anchor. To support a cable anywhere on a face, weld that face (set its bit). A cable that meets a face head-on (axis perpendicular to the face) is not anchored by it. A port-to-port run needs no frame if every cell is within 10 steps of a port-anchored end cell (at most 22 cells; the power study recommends 21 for margin).
frame_support_rules.face_tables: Each frame entry has 'faces': [{bit, face ('X+', 'Y-', ... or slope normal), verts_m}] in the prefab's local frame (metres, origin at the centre). Box frames: SC_FrameQuarterA / QuarterPorts / PortsCorner / QuarterPipe faces 0..5 = Y-, Y+, X+, Z+, X-, Z-; SC_FrameHalfA = Z+, Y+, Y-, X+, X-, Z-; SC_FrameA = X-, Z+ (triangle x=y side), Y+, Y-, Z+ (other triangle), X+, Z-, Z-. Example: 'Universal flight computer' welds bit 3 of a FrameHalfA at orientation 5 = local X+ = world -y, i.e. a welded floor under the logic.

glass_encasing.what: 'Glass-encased' logic: glass blocks are placed over (overlapping) the logic volume, so the parts sit inside the glass. The blueprint simply has overlapping records and the game loads them. Only the I/O cable ends and their labels stay outside.
glass_encasing.better_than_pid: 'Better Than PID. No tuning required . All planets': one SC_GlassHalfA at orientation 8, origin (196,20,204), world box x 196-199, y 20-23, z 204-211 (4x4x8). Inside: 9 logic parts, 41 of 45 cable cells and 3 small labels. Outside: 4 straight cable ends at z = 203 and 3 Large Labels at z = 199..202 (orientation 10). Glass _col = 15.
glass_encasing.universal_flight_computer: 'Universal flight computer. Plug and play by Santxc': three SC_GlassHalfA (orientations 8, 12, 8) side by side along x (origins x = 212, 216, 220; y 12-15; z 176-183; total 12x4x8) and three SC_FrameHalfA with exactly the same origins and boxes (orientations 5, 1, 5): 'double-encased'. Inside: 26 logic parts and 117 of 133 cable cells; cable ends one cell outside both z faces (z = 175 and 184), 18 Large Labels beyond them. Glass _col = 15; frames _col0..5 = 2, _col6..7 = 200; the first frame has _solidFaces = 0x08 (bit 3 = local X+ = world -y: a welded floor), the other two are bare.
glass_encasing.geometry: SC_GlassHalfA and SC_FrameHalfA are 4x8x4 with the 8 along local y. To lay the 8 along a world axis A, pick k with R_k*(0,1,0) = +-A: world z: 8 or 12 (glass), 1 or 5 (as used for the frames; these also put local x = world -y, so face bit 3 is the floor); world y: 16; world x: e.g. 18. The block's origin is the min corner of the world box, so tiles sit at multiples of 4 (short axes) and 8 (long axis) from the logic box's min corner.
glass_encasing.recipe: 1) Build the logic so that it fills whole 4x4x8 tiles (pad the box to multiples of 4/4/8). 2) Add one SC_GlassHalfA per tile, same box as the tile. 3) Optional double-encasing: one SC_FrameHalfA per tile with the same origin and box; weld its floor face if the logic rests on it (bit of the face that points world down). 4) Run each I/O cable one cell out of the glass (the end cell straight, open outward) and label it beyond the end (label_rules.placement_at_cable_ends). The pasted module's outer cells must rest on something when placed in a ship (the examples' labels and glass sit on the ship floor). 5) Frames/glass overlapping logic are the deliberate glitch: do not count those overlaps as collisions, but nothing else may overlap.
glass_encasing.other_examples: 'MEGA', 'Cruiser' and 'Somethin' contain a similar flight computer encased in two FrameHalfA (orientations 19 and 23, no glass).

_actionableLabel.meaning: label text, UTF-16LE, zero-padded to 32 bytes. Game _maxLength = 16 characters for this label (EPC_Actionable_Label in the prefab); corpus max = 16. Corpus text is upper case only (A-Z 0-9 space and %+,-./:).

_labelRotated.meaning: 0 = text upright with its top toward local +y; 1 = text turned 180 deg in the plate (top toward local -y). Older saves (56-byte record) lack the field (= 0). Declared 4 bytes but only byte 53 is the flag; write 0/1 there, zeros after.

attach.meaning: the label is a 0.02 m plate lying against its back face (local -z); its only JointsArea is that face, so the cells behind it (local z = -1) must hold the part it is mounted on (frame, logic block, ...).

text.reads_along: -x (first character at local x = 3 end) when _labelRotated = 0; +x when 1
